# Q5
To show that test MSE of model $Y = f(x) + \epsilon$,
$$
\E[(Y_0 - \hat{f}(x_0))^2] = \var(\hat{f}(x_0)) + b_f (\hat{f}(x_0))^2 + \var(\epsilon)
$$

We could write the expression of test MSE first,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\E[(Y_0 - \hat{f}(x_0))^2] 
&= \E[(f(x_0) + \epsilon - \hat{f}(x_0))^2] \\
&= \E[((f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)) + \epsilon )^2] \\
&= \E[(f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)^2] + 2\E[(f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)] \E[\epsilon] + \E[\epsilon^2]
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\epsilon$ is a random error term that is independent of $x$ and has mean zero, so
$$
E[\epsilon] = 0, \quad \var(\epsilon) = \E[\epsilon^2]
$$

Substitute the formulas into the derived test MSE expression,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\E[(Y_0 - \hat{f}(x_0))^2] 
&= \E[(f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)^2] + 2\E[(f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)] \cdot 0 + \var(\epsilon) \\
&= \E[(f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)^2] + \var(\epsilon)
\end{aligned}
$$
To further prove the result, we transform $f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)$ as follows.
$$
f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0) = (f(x_0) - \E[\hat{f}(x_0)]) + (\E[\hat{f}(x_0)] - \hat{f}(x_0))
$$

Substitute to $\E[(f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)^2]$, we can obtain that,
$$
\E[(f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0))^2] = 
\E[(\E[\hat{f}(x_0)] - \hat{f}(x_0))^2] + 
\E[(f(x_0) - E[\hat{f}(x_0)])^2] +
2\E[(\E[\hat{f}(x_0)] - \hat{f}(x_0))(f(x_0) - E[\hat{f}(x_0)])]
$$

Once more,  $\epsilon$ is a random error term that is independent of $x$ and has mean zero, so
$$
\E[\hat{f}(x_0)] 
= \E[f(x_0) + \epsilon] 
= \E[f(x_0)] + \E[\epsilon]
= f(x_0)
$$
So we can infer that $2\E[(\E[\hat{f}(x_0)] - \hat{f}(x_0))(f(x_0) - E[\hat{f}(x_0)])] = 0$.  
According to the property of variance and the definition of bias,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\var(\hat{f}(x_0)) &= \E[(\E[\hat{f}(x_0)] - \hat{f}(x_0))^2], \\
b_f(\hat{f}(x_0))^2 &= (f(x_0) - E[\hat{f}(x_0)])^2 = E[(f(x_0) - E[\hat{f}(x_0)])^2]
\end{aligned}
$$

So the equation could be written by
$$
\begin{aligned}
\E[(Y_0 - \hat{f}(x_0))^2] 
&= \E[(f(x_0) - \hat{f}(x_0)^2] + \var(\epsilon) \\
&= \var(\hat{f}(x_0)) + b_f(\hat{f}(x_0))^2 + \var(\epsilon)
\end{aligned}
$$
